author: WP10
summary: In the working tree this unit is a short overview of the four native and portable 2D families (SDL_RENDERER, DIRECT2D, GDI, FREEDIRECT) and their shared negative contract; its older retired-family content was removed before the synchronisation. All claims are current at 009d40f5 (one mechanism corrected: FREEDIRECT's shadow backbuffer). The renderers guide already had the scope, gates and 3D-call behaviour; the per-family presentation and conversion facts and the public-route testing rule were added as an expansion of the graphics backends internals page.

concepts.text: SDL_RENDERER, DIRECT2D, GDI and FREEDIRECT deliberately stop at a 2D contract (ThreeD false); they are not incomplete 3D renderers but smaller dependency or compatibility boundaries for SpriteBatch, SpriteFont, Texture2D and bounded render-target work.

SDL_RENDERER uploads textures as SDL_PIXELFORMAT_RGBA32 SDL textures and draws sprites through SDL_RenderTexture, SDL_RenderTextureRotated and SDL_RenderTextureAffine; it has no programmable 3D stage, depth/stencil buffer or MSAA contract, and reads back with SDL_RenderReadPixels.
Unsupported 3D factories and draws on SDL_RENDERER fail at a predictable seam: Unsupported3DGraphicsCallBehavior::Throw by default, WarnAndStub on request, instead of returning inert objects.

SDL_RENDERER's focused tests cover sorting, transforms, tint and blend, render-target use, pixel transfer and the negative capability boundary, including the shared unsupported-3D-call fixture registered for it.

DIRECT2D issues all drawing through ID2D1DeviceContext on a private Direct3D 11 device (hardware, with a WARP path forced by CNA_DIRECT2D_FORCE_WARP) that no application code can reach; it is not an application-visible Direct3D renderer.

DIRECT2D converts public RGBA bytes to tight BGRA at the upload boundary and back on readback, bounds bitmaps by GetMaximumBitmapSize() and refuses a mipmapped RenderTarget2D and every 3D route by name.

GDI reuses the Software family's CPU SpriteBatch and texturing core and presents the RGBA8 frame to a Win32 window with SetDIBitsToDevice in dirty bands, a genuine GDI presentation path with no OpenGL or Direct3D device.

GDI's recorded evidence comes from MinGW cross-builds run under Wine; native Windows lifecycle, DPI and physical-display behaviour remain separate, and the native gdi-windows-ci.yml workflow is manual dispatch only.

FREEDIRECT presents a DirectDraw-shaped 2D interface implemented by the separately pinned free-direct sibling (which uses SDL3 internally); CNA sees COM-shaped IDirectDrawSurface operations, and SDL is not part of CNA's renderer contract.
tokens: DirectDraw-shaped 2D renderer on the sibling free-direct reimplementation

concepts.text: FREEDIRECT composites Clear and every sprite into a lockable off-screen shadow backbuffer sized to the logical resolution, because the free-direct primary surface never exposes a writable pointer; Present() is one identity Blt() from it and readback locks the active surface.
concepts.note: The book said CPU shadows support public transfer; TARGET's mechanism is a lockable off-screen DirectDraw surface owned by the renderer.

concepts.text: 3D resources, custom effects and occlusion queries are outside FREEDIRECT's scope: all 19 capability answers except AdditiveBlending are false.
A 2D family must report no 3D capability, reject incompatible depth, format or MSAA requests and never accept a draw it will silently discard.
tokens: a draw is never accepted and silently discarded

concepts.text: The negative contract must be tested through the public resource and the public draw route: a unit test of an internal format or state mapper does not prove that GraphicsDevice refuses the operation safely.
tokens: through the public resource and the public draw route
